items.title: 68003_Eddie Sauter oral history interview
items.q: it all came about from getting to know Joe in that period

ctx.x: We also played with that band Ben Martin's Riviera at the Jersey shore. In that band was Tootie Camarata, who became, I guess, a famous pops conductor later on. And Chris Griffin who was a trumpet player at CBS for many, many years; Joe Moody. He wasn't directly involved in that one but it all came about from getting to know Joe in that period; he had his own group.

Tootie got a job with Charlie Barnet and got me in there and at that point I left Columbia. I had begun to take lessons-- the first lessons were with Archie Bleyer, and there was a guy named Billie Fisher--there was a Scott Fisher too at that time--I don't know if it does anything to you. They had a band, a North Jersey band, Billie was a precocious sort of saxophone player and arranger. He became an arranger for CBS for many, many years; he had gotten very commercial. I'm trying to remember the connection.
